introduced.explain: in `errorCondition`: no declared element matches `/Storefront/NoSuchField`, and no model-wide field short name resolved it

corrective.fix: The group or field name in the condition could not be resolved in the rule's scope. Use its ABSOLUTE path (a leading `/`, e.g. `/Order/Items/Sku`) rather than a bare or relative name — a bare name binds against the rule's OWN group first, and reaches ANY other group (an ancestor's field included: there is no upward search) only through the model-wide fallback, which needs `fieldRefByShortNameAllowed` AND a unique match. If the name is already correct, check the rule's iteration scope contains it: a per-row field needs the rule to iterate over its repeatable group (set the rule group to that group's PARENT, error field inside).
corrective.meaning: MVK_INVALID_ENTITY ("the group or field 'X' is not valid") means the kernel could not resolve that name — almost always a bare/relative reference that does not bind across sibling groups, or a field outside the rule's iteration scope.

gaps.reason: a field type's body is judged on the member A12 constructs from and on the two CONTENT laws measured beyond it — a `DateRangeType`'s (format, separator) pair, and an `EnumerationType`'s values against its categories. What a member otherwise holds is left to A12: a declared `format` outside the admitted vocabulary is refused there and cannot be reported here, since the admitted set is explicitly not closed and the refused one is a probe's universe rather than a law; a `CustomFieldType`'s `name` has no measured content law at all

the condition parser checks the SHAPE the grammar's productions share — a call is a name and a parenthesised argument list — and not each operator's own argument arity or operand kinds, so a call with the wrong number or kind of arguments is left to A12. Reproducing those per operator would be a second copy of the catalog, and every place the copy disagreed would refuse a condition A12 admits. A12's illegal-CHARACTER class IS reported, derived from the lexer's terminals, with one exception: a lone `#` is measured illegal and left alone, because `#Zeile`'s other language spellings are unknown here and refusing an unpaired `#` could reject text A12 accepts

two entity filters sharing ONE argument list are treated as separate connective levels without a measurement saying they are — `SumOfProducts` is the only operator whose argument list takes two entity specs and it refuses a filter on either for a reason of its own, so no oracle for that shape exists. This is silence rather than a wrong verdict

a computation that READS its own computed field is refused by A12 and is not reported here: a projected read draws a different class than a plain one, and a derived-scale mismatch in the same operation pre-empts both — neither is decidable without inferring an operation's scale, which this checker does not do. Re-open when it can
only the families named by `CheckFamily` are implemented; every other required family of the pinned profile was not examined
